messages:
lina: Heads-up from today's sampling: FP8 looks great for most traffic but a small set of templates (codegen + long context) produce brittle logits around layer 18-21. I'm thinking about a 'precision-mux' concept: route different layers of the same request to different precisions dynamically. Want quick sanity check.

sam: Interesting. So rather than switching the whole request to INT8/FP16, you change precision per-layer during the forward pass? That has some hairy kernel/caching implications.

omar: Exactly. Idea: keep attention/computation in FP8 for first N layers, detect rising numeric stress, then transition middle layers to INT8/FP16 while keeping early KV in FP8. We can do per-layer dequant on the fly.

kevin: Questions: 1) how do we detect 'numeric stress' fast enough? 2) what's the cost of on-the-fly dequant/quant conversions per layer? 3) cache compatibility?

lina: For detection: cheap per-layer signals (activation scale drift, max_abs exceed threshold, gradient-like sudden change in norm). We only check these stats which we already emit for ops.

sam: Conversion cost: dequant of one KV slice is like ~0.2ms on CPU/GPU (rough ballpark). If we do this rarely (0.1-1% of requests) cost is tolerable. But we need to avoid breaking batching: all requests in a batch are at different precisions mid-run. That requires per-request masks to pick kernels.

omar: Kernel-side approach: implement a 'mixed-lane' kernel that takes a bitmask for lanes to interpret as FP8 vs INT8 vs FP16. This avoids separate batches. Might be moderately complex but more efficient than splintering batches.

kevin: Mixed-lane kernels sound promising. Ops: we need to add telemetry: per-request per-layer precision map and cost delta. Also expose a per-tenant precision budget so enterprise customers can opt into aggressive muxing.

lina: Cache question: prefer a canonical cache format on disk/network (float32) but allow in-memory compressed lanes. When a lane changes precision mid-run we rehydrate that lane's slice. We keep metadata: (lane_id, stored_format, scale).

sam: Edge cases: if we change precision for self-attention keys but not values, must ensure quant-dequant semantics are consistent. Also positional rotary embeddings quant noise could amplify. Need unit tests for cross-layer interactions.

omar: Safety: define a 'precision fence' concept. Once the fence is crossed (e.g., after layer 22), we stop further down-precisioning to avoid oscillation. Also add hysteresis: if we escalate to higher precision, don't return to lower for X tokens.

lina: Pseudocode for mux controller:

```
for layer in layers:
  stats = collect_layer_stats(layer)
  if stats.scale > SCALE_T or stats.max_abs > MAX_T:
    set_precision(layer+1:, HIGH)
    mark_fence(layer+FENCE_LEN)
    break
```

kevin: Deployment plan: start with a user-space shim that wraps model forward and injects per-layer decisions using existing kernels (convert in/out). Prototype perf and correctness. If promising, upstream kernel changes for mixed-lane support.

sam: Perf sim request: can you estimate expected p99 latency growth for three strategies: a) naive isolate-suspect to high-precision batch, b) mixed-lane kernels, c) upfront full-request escalation?

lina: Rough numbers from microbenchmarks: isolate-suspect adds 15-40ms p99 (depends on steal efficiency), mixed-lane adds ~5-12ms p99 (conversion overhead), full-request escalate adds ~40-70ms p99. Mixed-lane seems best tradeoff. We'll quantify on real traces.

omar: Quality tradeoff: we should measure per-layer influence score: which layers disproportionately affect final token distribution. Use gradient-based ablation or Fisher info proxies to prioritize layers for upscaling. That lets mux choose smallest set of layers to flip.

kevin: Ops controls: global budget (max N lane-changes per second), per-tenant budget, and emergency kill-switch if GPU saturation observed. Also, billing: reflect mixed-lane compute in cost breakdowns.

lina: UX: add request metadata `precision_mux: auto|aggressive|conservative` and return `precision_map: "L0-L10:FP8,L11-L14:INT8,L15-LN:FP16"` and `decision_reason`.

sam: One more: model-compatibility. Not all models behave well with mid-run precision flips (some have inter-layer fused ops). We need a compatibility matrix per model-version. Start by gating on verified models only.

omar: Action items: 1) lina to run per-layer ablation to compute influence scores on sample workloads (ETA 5d). 2) sam to prototype mixed-lane kernel perf microbench (ETA 1w). 3) kevin to design telemetry + budget enforcement + billing hooks (ETA 4d). 4) ops-bot to create ticket 'precision-mux-probe'.

ops-bot: Created ticket precision-mux-probe and assigned lina/sam/kevin. :white_check_mark:

lina: Great discussion. If microbenchmarks look sane we'll draft an RFC focused on kernel surface, cache format, and ops controls. Thanks all!
